title: Mansa Musa's 1324 Pilgrimage: The Journey That Redefined Mali
hook: When the richest man of his age set out with a mountain of gold, the world took notice—and the Sahara never looked the same.
logline: A single pilgrimage turns the humble empire of Mali into a legend, reshaping trade, faith, and global perception.

cast.name: Mansa Musa
cast.trait: generous to a fault, with a vision of divine legitimacy

cast.name: Karim al‑Farsi
cast.trait: meticulous organizer, keeps the camels in line

cast.name: Fatima bint Yusuf
cast.trait: sharp‑tongued trader who knows every market’s pulse

cast.name: Sankore the Scholar
cast.trait: eager to record the pilgrimage for posterity

cast.name: Courtier Jali
cast.trait: cautious, worries about the empire’s coffers

chapters.title: The Decision in Niani
chapters.purpose: Establish why Mansa Musa chooses a hajj and what he hopes to gain.
key_events: Musa declares his intention to fulfill the pilgrimage to Mecca.
Courtier Jali warns of the financial risk.
Sankore drafts a plan to document the journey as a legacy project.

chapters.title: Assembling the Golden Caravan
chapters.purpose: Show the scale of preparation and the symbolic weight of wealth.
key_events: Karim organizes thousands of camels, soldiers, and scholars.
Musa loads the caravan with gold, gifts, and a retinue of dignitaries.
Fatima negotiates trade permits for crossing the Sahara.

chapters.title: Crossing the Desert – Trials and Triumphs
chapters.purpose: Depict the hardships of the Sahara and the caravan’s growing reputation.
key_events: Musa’s generosity to oasis towns earns loyalty and fresh supplies.
Rumors of a “golden king” begin to spread among nomads.

chapters.title: Mecca and the Ripple Effect
chapters.purpose: Illustrate the pilgrimage’s climax and its immediate economic impact.
key_events: Musa performs the rites of hajj, drawing crowds of awe.
He distributes gold in Cairo, causing a temporary inflation.
Fatima secures new trade agreements for Mali’s gold, salt, and ivory.

chapters.title: Return and Re‑branding of Mali
chapters.purpose: Conclude with how the journey reshapes Mali’s global standing.
key_events: Musa returns to Niani with enhanced prestige and new diplomatic contacts.
Courtier Jali acknowledges the economic boost despite earlier doubts.
Sankore’s chronicles spread across the Islamic world, cementing Mali’s legend.

ending: Back in Niani, the emperor’s golden pilgrimage becomes the cornerstone of Mali’s identity—its wealth, piety, and cultural influence echoing through centuries, all recorded in the scholar’s ink‑stained scrolls.
